newsitem.title: JAPAN: Australia Deputy P.M. shortens Japan trip.
newsitem.headline: Australia Deputy P.M. shortens Japan trip.

text.p: Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Thursday he will cut short a visit to Japan because of a landslide in Australia's Snowy Mountains that may have killed up to 20 people.
He said he would visit the area at an appropriate time.
"I think the priority is the rescue effort," Fischer told reporters. "The state emergency services, the police, and, if the need arises, the defence forces are there."

Fischer said he would take part in Japan-Australia ministerial talks on Friday and return to Australia on Saturday, cancelling a scheduled climb of the famed Mount Fuji at the weekend. Fischer was originally scheduled to fly home Sunday evening.
Six Australian cabinet members, including Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, are attending the one-day ministerial meeting.

Two ski lodges at Thredbo, Australia's most popular ski resort, were crushed by a landslide just before midnight on Wednesday and rescue workers at the site on Thursday said they could not detect signs of life in the ruins.
Fischer said he heard about the disaster on Thursday and expressed sympathy for the families of the 20 people thought to have been trapped in the two lodges.
"I wish Godspeed to the rescue effort. I understand the complexity and the challenge represented by the very fragile situation on the side of the mountain," Fischer said.
"Let me say that the very famous spirit of the Snowy Mountains will help in the recovery situation."
